correctness.rationale: The scalar root objective is strictly convex because the root mass is positive, so each pooling chamber is well-defined. In root-to-leaf difference coordinates, the derivative deletes pooled rows and subtracts a mass-weighted pooled scalar on each unpooled row. The weighted ℓ1 matrix norm is its largest weighted absolute column sum. Every pooled column is bounded by its singleton-pooling analogue, which occurs in an open chamber; an unpooled chamber gives one. Piecewise-affine segment integration proves the global upper bound and short local segments give finite equality. Normalizing positive variation weights turns minimax into the exact scalar inequalities vi>=ti/(rho+ti), with a unique positive normalization root. The 280-instance exact-rational face test, 11,200 exact-rational pair checks and the explicit witness checks independently corroborate the formulas; unrestricted dimensions follow from proof, not experiment.

value.rationale: Weighted isotonic projection on a branching star is a canonical shape-constrained nonlinear map; its natural graph edge-variation sensitivity is not characterized by the known Euclidean nonexpansivity. The theorem gives sharp all-mass/all-weight constants, a necessary-and-sufficient mass-balance threshold for whether any positive edge metric makes the estimator nonexpansive, and a uniquely optimal stabilizing edge metric where amplification is unavoidable. For unit-mass leaves, the exact root-mass stability threshold is \(\mu_0\ge m-2\), which rules out all edge reweightings below that threshold. This structural design law is materially beyond the already known uniform-star specialization and identifies exactly how root mass can suppress branch-induced perturbation amplification.
